questions.question: What are three (3) examples of risks potentially associated with gaining access to an event venue or site?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Locked gates or doors
Lack of venue/site staff to give direction
Blocked or busy access roads
Driveways or entry points unable to accommodate dimensions of vehicles requiring access
Drivers/personnel don’t know where to go
Crowded entry points slowing down access
Too many vehicles.
answer_instructions: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
answer_points: Locked gates or doors
Lack of venue/site staff to give direction
Blocked or busy access roads
Driveways or entry points unable to accommodate dimensions of vehicles requiring access
Drivers/personnel don’t know where to go
Crowded entry points slowing down access
Too many vehicles.

questions.question: What are three (3) examples of methods that may be applied to manage risks associated with gaining access to an event venue or site?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Make access arrangements with venue/site management
Obtain keys
Measure access to ensure vehicles will fit, or to decide the maximum dimensions of vehicles that can be used
Obtain permits to close streets etc if necessary
Distribute information sheets to those needing access providing them with directions and contact details of personnel who can assist
Schedule access times to avoid bottlenecks
Restrict access to required vehicles only.
answer_instructions: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
answer_points: Make access arrangements with venue/site management
Obtain keys
Measure access to ensure vehicles will fit, or to decide the maximum dimensions of vehicles that can be used
Obtain permits to close streets etc if necessary
Distribute information sheets to those needing access providing them with directions and contact details of personnel who can assist
Schedule access times to avoid bottlenecks
Restrict access to required vehicles only.

questions.question: What are three (3) examples of risks and regulatory issues potentially associated with liquor licensing for an event at a venue or site?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Licence or permit may not be in place
Licence or permit may not allow for delivery of event service requirements
Licence or permit may not allow contracted service times to be met
Licence or permit terms and conditions may be difficult to comply with
No one is available to assume the responsibilities of the licensee
Staff not trained in RSA.
answer_instructions: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
answer_points: Licence or permit may not be in place
Licence or permit may not allow for delivery of event service requirements
Licence or permit may not allow contracted service times to be met
Licence or permit terms and conditions may be difficult to comply with
No one is available to assume the responsibilities of the licensee
Staff not trained in RSA.

questions.question: What are three (3) examples of methods that may be applied to manage risks and regulatory issues associated with liquor licensing obligations for an event venue or site?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Contact liquor authorities and seek their guidance on licence/permit requirements
Apply for licence/permit early using the required forms and paying the prescribed fee
Nominate a person to be responsible (as a licensee or other)
Ensure a copy of the licence/permit is available at the event
Require all liquor service staff to provide a copy of the current RSA certificate and keep it in a folder at the event for inspection by police/authorities if needed
Post required signage at strategic locations around the venue/site
Strictly enforce RSA principles.

questions.question: What are three (3) examples of risks potentially associated with coordinating contractors used to deliver an event at a venue or site?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Contractors unsure of what to do or provide
Contractors want to do their own thing and ignore event requirements/specifications
Contractors unsure of when to provide items/services
Contractors do not know what other contractors are doing so that activities can be properly and most effectively scheduled
Contractors unsure of standards that apply to the work they perform
Contractors are not paid retainers, deposits or progress payments.
answer_instructions: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
answer_points: Contractors unsure of what to do or provide
Contractors want to do their own thing and ignore event requirements/specifications
Contractors unsure of when to provide items/services
Contractors do not know what other contractors are doing so that activities can be properly and most effectively scheduled
Contractors unsure of standards that apply to the work they perform
Contractors are not paid retainers, deposits or progress payments.

questions.question: What are three (3) examples of methods that may be applied to manage risks associated with the coordination of contractors who work on an event at a given venue or site?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Communicate often and in writing as well as verbally
Provide them with mandatory briefings
Distribute the schedule of contracted works – start and finish days and times
Create and share a copy of required/agreed work standards
Provide contractors with contact details of other contractors
Nominate one point of contact for contractor enquiries
Pay retainers, deposits or progress payments and keep proof of payment in an event folder on-site.

Provide contractors with contact details of other contractors

questions.question: What are three (3) examples of methods that may be applied to manage physical constraint issues for an event at a given venue or site?

Use or identify the supplementary supplier
Hire/rent items
Clean and/or repair/maintain items
Substitute items for an acceptable alternative.

questions.question: What are three (3) examples of venue or site appeal risks for an intended audience at an event venue or site?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Location does not meet attendee expectations
Venue or site lacks attractiveness or ambience
Adverse weather conditions
Location is unclean and untidy.

questions.question: What are three (3) examples of venue or site crowd control risks at an event venue or site?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Crowds are slow in moving from entry points to allocated seating
Crowd stampedes and/or crushes at any time but especially on arrival and departure
Long queue lines at entry points
Lack of attendee knowledge of where to go
Abusive and anti-social behaviour.

questions.question: What are three (3) examples of methods that may be applied to manage crowd control issues for an event at a given venue or site?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Liaise with police
Use paid uniformed police at the event
Use trained crowd controllers
Provide clear, numerous, overhead signage
Supplement crowd advice and directions using the PA system
Open more entry and departure points
Open entry points earlier
Prescribe structured queuing lines
Develop strategic crown management/control plans for on-arrival and on-departure crowds.
